subject: Post-demo recap: budget range, unit economics, and model allocation
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmeai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Thanks — a few follow-ups on pricing & usage profile

Vanessa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it gave our product and infra teams a good sense of Redwood's runtimes and ops. A few follow-ups so we can get internal approval to move to pilot: 

1) Expected volumes (high-level):
   - Generative chat (user messages + assistant tokens): ~500M tokens / month
   - Embeddings: ~2M vectors / month (100 tokens equivalent per call on average)
   - Reranking calls (short inputs): ~50M tokens / month

2) Budget range: procurement asked for a target unit economics line — ideally a rough target $/1M tokens so we can compare to our current third-party spend. Our CFO said budget band of $5k–$12k per month for an initial pilot evaluation, but long-term we expect to scale.

3) Model mix question: we want to understand if you expect the 500M chat tokens to be split across multiple model sizes (chat-xxx / chat-yyy) and if embeddings will be on a different model family — any recommended mix for cost/latency tradeoffs?

Can you send a short recap with illustrative per-1M-token numbers and a suggested model allocation that maps to the volumes above? If you can also attach a pricing sheet we can circulate, that would help.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: Re: Thanks — a few follow-ups on pricing & usage profile

Hi Liam — great to chat. Quick recap below and an initial set of unit economics and model-allocation recommendations. I attached a short pricing scenarios workbook (pricing-scenarios-ACME.xlsx) and the demo one-pager.

Summary of assumptions (based on today's call):
- Chat total: 500M tokens / month (we'll assume 60% prompt / 40% completion split)
- Embeddings: 2M vectors / month — we'll treat these as batched embed RPCs (avg 100 tokens equivalent)
- Rerank: 50M tokens / month (short contexts, lower completion size)

Suggested model allocation (cost vs. quality):
- Chat workload (500M):
  * chat-medium (recommended for bulk user messages): 70% of chat tokens (~350M) — best cost/quality for typical assistant responses
  * chat-large (higher quality for priority flows / payment/checkout/billing): 20% (~100M)
  * chat-xxs (system prompts, short confirmations, caching-friendly): 10% (~50M)
- Embeddings: use the embeddings-medium family for 100% of vector work (2M vectors) — recommend batching at 128 vectors/batch to reduce token-equivalent overhead
- Rerank: lightweight reranker model (rerank-small) for the 50M tokens — keep these on separate pool for latency predictability

Illustrative unit economics (list prices, pre-volume discounts):
- chat-medium: $9.50 per 1M tokens
- chat-large: $23.00 per 1M tokens
- chat-xxs: $3.20 per 1M tokens
- embeddings-medium: $45 per 1M vector-equivalents (we normalize to token-equivalent in the spreadsheet)
- rerank-small: $2.75 per 1M tokens

Estimated monthly spend (no committed discount applied):
- Chat-medium: 350M / 1M * $9.50 = $3,325
- Chat-large: 100M / 1M * $23.00 = $2,300
- Chat-xxs: 50M / 1M * $3.20 = $160
- Rerank-small: 50M / 1M * $2.75 = $137.50
- Embeddings (normalized): 2M vectors -> normalized cost line in attached sheet = ~$90

Total est. list spend: ~$6,012.50 / month (~$72k / year).

Target $/1M tokens metric (more useful for procurement comparisons):
- Blended target (based on suggested mix): ~$6.00 per 1M tokens (this is the blended rate across chat+rerank when you normalize embeddings to token-equivalent and weight by volume).

Notes and levers to reduce cost:
- Commit/Reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) can reduce the blended $/1M to the $3.50–$4.50 range depending on term and uplift for guaranteed latency.
- Quantization and smaller model mix: increase chat-medium share and offload low-value flows to chat-xxs to push blended cost down ~10–15%.
- Batch embeddings aggressively to reduce per-vector overhead in the sheet.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll follow up with a short, formal quote and two pricing scenarios: (A) 3-month pilot (no commit) at list rates, (B) 12-month reserved capacity with a discount schedule.
2) Karthik / Marissa will prep a brief SOW template if you want to move to pilot.
3) Can we schedule a 30-min procurement call to align on PO timing? Marissa, can you suggest 2x times tomorrow or Wed?

If that looks reasonable I'll get the quote into HubSpot and you can share with your CFO.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Liam — adding a few operational notes that align to Vanessa's costing above:

- If you expect steady-state 500M tokens with predictable diurnal patterns we can recommend a reserved Dedicated pool for the chat-medium family. That is the primary lever to bring blended $/1M under $5.
- For the embeddings we recommend a small reserved pool that supports batched RPCs; the billing in the sheet shows how batching reduces the effective tokens-per-vector.
- We'll include a pilot SLA (uptime, latency p50/p95) in the SOW and an optional automatic fallback policy to a compatible model variant if capacity is constrained.

Action items from Redwood:
- Vanessa: formal quote with (Pilot / Reserved) scenarios into HubSpot by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: draft SOW and provide standard pilot terms + proposed SLA.
- Acme: confirm whether procurement needs a PO for pilot, and if finance wants the blended $/1M framed as an annualized figure.

Happy to jump on a 30-min procurement sync — I'm available tomorrow 10:30–11:30am ET or Wed 2–4pm ET.

Thanks,
Karthik
